title: gov.uk: the first £1,000 of property income is tax free, so £900 of rent gives no taxable profit
working: Rent 900 is below the 1,000 property allowance.

title: gov.uk: profit is rent less allowable expenses; £12,000 of rent less £3,000 of expenses is £9,000, taxed at the basic rate on top of £30,000 of pay, £1,800 in 2026/27
working: Expenses 3,000 exceed the 1,000 allowance so they are used. Profit 9,000. Pay uses the allowance; 17,430 + 9,000 = 26,430 stays within the 37,700 basic rate limit. 9,000 x 20% = 1,800.

title: gov.uk: the £1,000 allowance is used instead of £400 of expenses, since they cannot both be deducted
Budget 2026: the same £9,000 of profit is charged at the 24% property basic rate from April 2027, £2,160
Budget 2026: profit that straddles the basic rate limit is split between the 24% and 44% property rates, in Wales as in England
gov.uk: in 2026/27 rental profit for a Scottish taxpayer is taxed at the Scottish rates; £9,000 on top of £30,000 of pay is in the intermediate rate band at 21%
working: Pay above the allowance 17,430 sits in the Scottish basic rate band (up to 16,956 taxable is basic; 17,430 is already intermediate). Profit 9,000 from 17,430 to 26,430 is all within the intermediate band (16,957 to 31,092) at 21% = 1,890.
